Alex: Quick signal — after yesterday's routing policy tweak I'm seeing p95 < p50 for /v1/generate in eu-west. p95=120ms, p50=250ms. Not adding up. :eyes:
Priya: Huh. Can you share the metric query/window you used?
Alex: Sure — here's what I ran locally: ```SELECT percentile(response_ms, 0.95) AS p95, percentile(response_ms, 0.5) AS p50, COUNT(*) AS sample_count, sample_origin FROM requests WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND region='eu-west' AND ts > now()-1h GROUP BY sample_origin;```
Ben: My bet: routing created a big cohort routed to the fast-cache fallback with very low latencies. If rollups merge origins without accounting for sample weights, percentiles can be pulled down.
Sam: So two possibilities: policy routed more traffic to fast-cache (expected), or the telemetry aggregation dropped/normalized sample weights during the rollup. Which one looks true?
Alex: Telemetry dump shows raw counts: ingress=2k, backend=300, fast-cache=16k (raw sampled). But effective logical traffic after sampling/instrumentation: ingress~2k, backend~300, fast-cache~2k. So raw proportions and effective weights disagree.
Priya: That mismatch would definitely break unweighted t-digest merges. Do we carry sample_count or sample_weight in our rollup metadata?
Ben: Historically we only merged tdigests and carried a 'count' field that reflected raw observed samples, not the origin-corrected logical weight. After routing fallthroughs this surfaces as an inversion.
Sam: Short term UX fix: show "sample_count" and an "origin breakdown" overlay on the percentile chart so engineers can see if one origin dominates raw samples. Also add a tiny tooltip explaining difference between raw samples vs effective traffic.
Priya: Medium term: change rollup semantics to propagate an explicit sample_weight per entry and do weight-aware merges of tdigests (or carry raw + effective counts).
Alex: Also proposing a guardrail: fire an automation/warning if p95 < p50 for a given endpoint/time-slice (or if ordering flips by more than X ms). It should surface the likely cause: sampling mismatch vs real latency regression.
Ben: Agree. I'll sketch the aggregator change: carry a map {origin: effective_count} in rollup metadata and use it to reweight tdigests before computing global percentiles. That keeps downstream UI cheaper.
Priya: Can you add a small reproducible query to the runbook? e.g., compute percentiles per-origin vs merged to show the inversion: ```WITH per_origin AS (SELECT sample_origin, percentile(response_ms,0.95) p95, percentile(response_ms,0.5) p50, count(*) c FROM requests WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND ts > now()-1h GROUP BY sample_origin) SELECT * FROM per_origin;```
Alex: Done — I'll add the runbook note and a quick dashboard panel that shows p50/p95 by origin side-by-side and total merged pctl.
TelemetryBot: Created incident INC-2026-023: "routing-fallback-sample-weight-bias". Tasks: add sample_count badge, inversion alert, aggregator PR. Link: https://redwood/internal/inc/INC-2026-023
Alex: I'll open PR for the console badge + alert: `github.com/redwood/console/pull/891` and for the aggregator change: `github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/4321`. Please review.
Priya: I'll review both today. Also let's ping eng-runtime + eng-releases before the next routing rollout so this doesn't surprise SRE/PS.
Ben: Good call. Also note in the release notes: "routing policy can change raw sample composition; console will now show sample provenance to avoid percentile inversion confusion."
Sam: Thanks — and short-term thumbs-up for the dashboard panel. :thumbsup:
